nl:
An air-traffic control center runs two independent controller instances that both hand out landing slots from one shared pool of runways. To keep the two instances from acting on stale authority, the center uses an epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme: a global epoch counter is bumped whenever authority is reassigned, and each controller separately learns (syncs) the current epoch over time. A controller is allowed to allocate a runway only while the epoch it currently believes matches the live global epoch; a controller that has fallen behind is considered stale and must re-sync first. When a runway is allocated the center records the epoch under which the allocation was made. Reconfiguration can happen at any time, so a controller that was current a moment ago may become stale. A controller may release a runway it holds at any time. The danger to guard against is a lagging controller quietly allocating runways on outdated authority.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every runway that is currently allocated was granted under an epoch no greater than the epoch its owning controller presently knows, so no controller holds a slot it took while stale.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m9p6t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Controllers, Runways, MaxEpoch
ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat

VARIABLES gepoch, ctrlEpoch, owner, ownerEpoch
vars == <<gepoch, ctrlEpoch, owner, ownerEpoch>>

NoOwner == "free"

TypeOK ==
    /\ gepoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ ctrlEpoch \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ owner \in [Runways -> Controllers \cup {NoOwner}]
    /\ ownerEpoch \in [Runways -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ gepoch = 0
    /\ ctrlEpoch = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [r \in Runways |-> NoOwner]
    /\ ownerEpoch = [r \in Runways |-> 0]

\* Authority is reassigned: bump the global epoch and let one controller
\* learn the new value immediately (the others fall behind and go stale).
Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ gepoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ gepoch' = gepoch + 1
    /\ ctrlEpoch' = [ctrlEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = gepoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ownerEpoch>>

\* A lagging controller catches up to the live epoch.
Sync(c) ==
    /\ ctrlEpoch[c] < gepoch
    /\ ctrlEpoch' = [ctrlEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = gepoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gepoch, owner, ownerEpoch>>

\* A controller allocates a free runway ONLY while it is current, recording
\* the live epoch on the runway.
Allocate(c, r) ==
    /\ owner[r] = NoOwner
    /\ ctrlEpoch[c] = gepoch
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ ownerEpoch' = [ownerEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = gepoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gepoch, ctrlEpoch>>

\* A controller frees a runway it holds.
Release(c, r) ==
    /\ owner[r] = c
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![r] = NoOwner]
    /\ ownerEpoch' = [ownerEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gepoch, ctrlEpoch>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Sync(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : Allocate(c, r)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : Release(c, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No controller holds a slot it took while stale: the epoch recorded on a
\* held runway never exceeds what its owner currently knows.
NoStaleHold ==
    \A r \in Runways :
        owner[r] # NoOwner => ownerEpoch[r] <= ctrlEpoch[owner[r]]
=============================================================================

nl:
A network of vending machines is restocked by roaming service agents who must take a short lease on a machine slot before refilling it. A lease carries an expiry: it is granted for a fixed number of clock ticks and lapses when the clock passes that deadline. An agent acquires a slot only when the slot is unowned or its current lease has already lapsed, and acquiring an expired slot evicts whatever stale claim the previous holder still carried. Agents may renew a lease they still hold, and may release it when done. A back-office admin holds a privileged override that can forcibly clear any slot and cancel every agent's claim on it, for example to pull a malfunctioning machine. The clock only moves forward. The hazard to prevent is two different agents both believing they hold the very same slot at the same moment.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct agents ever simultaneously hold a claim on the same vending slot.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m6p3t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Agents, Slots, MaxClock, LeaseLen
ASSUME MaxClock \in Nat /\ LeaseLen \in Nat

VARIABLES clock, owner, expiry, claim
vars == <<clock, owner, expiry, claim>>

Nobody == "nobody"
NoSlot == "noslot"

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Agents \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ expiry \in [Slots -> 0..(MaxClock + LeaseLen)]
    /\ claim \in [Agents -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Nobody]
    /\ expiry = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ claim = [a \in Agents |-> NoSlot]

Lapsed(s) == owner[s] = Nobody \/ expiry[s] <= clock

\* Acquire a free or lapsed slot; acquiring evicts any stale claim on it.
Acquire(a, s) ==
    /\ claim[a] = NoSlot
    /\ Lapsed(s)
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = a]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ claim' = [x \in Agents |->
                    IF x = a THEN s
                    ELSE IF claim[x] = s THEN NoSlot
                    ELSE claim[x]]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* Extend a lease the agent still legitimately holds.
Renew(a, s) ==
    /\ claim[a] = s
    /\ owner[s] = a
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, owner, claim>>

\* Voluntarily give up a held slot.
Release(a, s) ==
    /\ claim[a] = s
    /\ owner[s] = a
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![a] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry>>

\* The privileged admin forcibly clears a slot and cancels all claims on it.
AdminOverride(s) ==
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
    /\ claim' = [x \in Agents |-> IF claim[x] = s THEN NoSlot ELSE claim[x]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, expiry, claim>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents, s \in Slots : Acquire(a, s)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, s \in Slots : Renew(a, s)
    \/ \E a \in Agents, s \in Slots : Release(a, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminOverride(s)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Two distinct agents never hold a claim on the same slot at once.
NoDoubleClaim ==
    \A a, b \in Agents :
        (claim[a] # NoSlot /\ claim[a] = claim[b]) => a = b
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Agents = {a1, a2}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    MaxClock = 3
    LeaseLen = 2
INVARIANT NoDoubleClaim
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A power-grid load shedder is run by two independent controller instances that both draw on one shared set of grid nodes. Exclusive authority to move load onto a node circulates as a token on a ring: each instance holds its own token, and only the instance whose token currently sits on a node may act there. External demand accumulates at each node over time. When an instance is online and its token sits on a node with pending demand, it may shed one unit of that demand onto the node's load, but only while that node's load is still below the hard capacity. An instance may also relieve a node by pulling one unit of load back off. Instances can go offline and come back online. Because both instances share the same nodes, either or both may be pushing load onto the same node, so the capacity guard is the only thing standing between the grid and an overload.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The load placed on any grid node never exceeds its fixed capacity.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m1p4t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Instances, NodeCount, Cap, MaxReq
ASSUME NodeCount \in Nat /\ Cap \in Nat /\ MaxReq \in Nat

Nodes == 0..(NodeCount - 1)
Succ(n) == (n + 1) % NodeCount

VARIABLES tok, load, pending, online
vars == <<tok, load, pending, online>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ tok \in [Instances -> Nodes]
    /\ load \in [Nodes -> 0..(Cap + 2)]
    /\ pending \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxReq]
    /\ online \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ tok = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ load = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ pending = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ online = [i \in Instances |-> TRUE]

\* External demand piles up at a node.
RaiseDemand(n) ==
    /\ pending[n] < MaxReq
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![n] = pending[n] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, load, online>>

\* The token advances one step around the ring.
PassToken(i) ==
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![i] = Succ(tok[i])]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, pending, online>>

\* The token holder sheds one demand unit onto its node, respecting capacity.
Serve(i, n) ==
    /\ online[i]
    /\ tok[i] = n
    /\ pending[n] > 0
    /\ load[n] < Cap
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![n] = load[n] + 1]
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![n] = pending[n] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, online>>

\* The token holder relieves one unit of load from its node.
Relieve(i, n) ==
    /\ tok[i] = n
    /\ load[n] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![n] = load[n] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, pending, online>>

\* An instance drops offline or comes back.
Toggle(i) ==
    /\ online' = [online EXCEPT ![i] = ~online[i]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, load, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : RaiseDemand(n)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : PassToken(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, n \in Nodes : Serve(i, n)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, n \in Nodes : Relieve(i, n)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Toggle(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Capacity is never exceeded at any node.
BoundedCapacity == \A n \in Nodes : load[n] <= Cap
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    NodeCount = 2
    Cap = 2
    MaxReq = 2
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
An interbank settlement batch is posted through a single shared compare-and-swap register that carries a running batch value and a version number. Each participating bank works in two steps: it first reads the register's current version, then later attempts to commit its settlement, which only succeeds if the version it read still matches the register's live version. Between a bank's read and its commit, the central settlement engine may post its own authoritative update, which advances the version and leaves any bank that read earlier holding a stale version. Such a bank is slow, not failed: it is still running and may retry, but its outdated commit must be rejected rather than silently overwriting fresher state. A bank that notices it is behind can abort and drop its stale observation before reading again. Every successful write records the version its writer observed. The hazard is a lagging bank committing on a version that has already moved on.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever any write has occurred, the version observed by the most recent writer is exactly one less than the register's current version, so no stale writer ever committed.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m7p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Banks, MaxVer, Modulus
ASSUME MaxVer \in Nat /\ Modulus \in Nat

NoWriter == "none"
Engine == "engine"

VARIABLES regVal, regVer, observed, writerObs, lastWriter
vars == <<regVal, regVer, observed, writerObs, lastWriter>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ regVal \in 0..(Modulus - 1)
    /\ regVer \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ observed \in [Banks -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ writerObs \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ lastWriter \in Banks \cup {NoWriter, Engine}

Init ==
    /\ regVal = 0
    /\ regVer = 0
    /\ observed = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ writerObs = 0
    /\ lastWriter = NoWriter

\* A bank snapshots the current version.
Read(b) ==
    /\ observed' = [observed EXCEPT ![b] = regVer]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVal, regVer, writerObs, lastWriter>>

\* Compare-and-swap: the bank commits only if its snapshot is still live.
Commit(b) ==
    /\ regVer < MaxVer
    /\ observed[b] = regVer
    /\ regVal' = (regVal + 1) % Modulus
    /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
    /\ writerObs' = observed[b]
    /\ lastWriter' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED observed

\* The authoritative settlement engine posts an update, moving the version on.
EnginePost ==
    /\ regVer < MaxVer
    /\ regVal' = (regVal + 2) % Modulus
    /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
    /\ writerObs' = regVer
    /\ lastWriter' = Engine
    /\ UNCHANGED observed

\* A bank that fell behind discards its stale snapshot.
Abort(b) ==
    /\ observed[b] # 0
    /\ observed[b] < regVer
    /\ observed' = [observed EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVal, regVer, writerObs, lastWriter>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Read(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Commit(b)
    \/ EnginePost
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Abort(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stale writer ever committed: the last writer observed the version just
\* prior to the one it installed.
NoStaleCommit ==
    lastWriter # NoWriter => writerObs = regVer - 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    MaxVer = 3
    Modulus = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleCommit
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A university course-registration system is served by two independent front-end instances that share one common pool of course seats. To serialize their writes, a single registration token circulates on a ring between the instances, and only the instance currently holding the token may change enrollment. Each course starts with a fixed number of seats, split at all times between free seats and enrolled seats. The token holder may enroll a student into a course that still has a free seat, moving one seat from free to enrolled, or drop a student, moving one seat back. When a course is full a student may join its waitlist instead, and when a free seat later appears a waitlisted student can be promoted directly into it. Whatever the two instances do, the physical seats of a course are neither created nor destroyed: every seat is always accounted for as either free or enrolled. The hazard is a bookkeeping slip that makes seats appear or vanish.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every course, the number of free seats plus the number of enrolled seats always equals its fixed capacity.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m1p2t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Courses, InstCount, Cap, MaxWL
ASSUME InstCount \in Nat /\ Cap \in Nat /\ MaxWL \in Nat

Instances == 0..(InstCount - 1)
NextInst(i) == (i + 1) % InstCount

VARIABLES tok, enrolled, free, waitlist
vars == <<tok, enrolled, free, waitlist>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ tok \in Instances
    /\ enrolled \in [Courses -> 0..Cap]
    /\ free \in [Courses -> 0..Cap]
    /\ waitlist \in [Courses -> 0..MaxWL]

Init ==
    /\ tok = 0
    /\ enrolled = [c \in Courses |-> 0]
    /\ free = [c \in Courses |-> Cap]
    /\ waitlist = [c \in Courses |-> 0]

\* The registration token advances to the next instance on the ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ tok' = NextInst(tok)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, free, waitlist>>

\* The token holder enrolls a student, consuming one free seat.
Enroll(i, c) ==
    /\ tok = i
    /\ free[c] > 0
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![c] = enrolled[c] + 1]
    /\ free' = [free EXCEPT ![c] = free[c] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, waitlist>>

\* The token holder drops a student, returning one free seat.
Drop(i, c) ==
    /\ tok = i
    /\ enrolled[c] > 0
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![c] = enrolled[c] - 1]
    /\ free' = [free EXCEPT ![c] = free[c] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, waitlist>>

\* A student joins the waitlist of a full course.
JoinWaitlist(c) ==
    /\ free[c] = 0
    /\ waitlist[c] < MaxWL
    /\ waitlist' = [waitlist EXCEPT ![c] = waitlist[c] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, enrolled, free>>

\* A waitlisted student is promoted into a freshly opened seat.
Promote(i, c) ==
    /\ tok = i
    /\ waitlist[c] > 0
    /\ free[c] > 0
    /\ waitlist' = [waitlist EXCEPT ![c] = waitlist[c] - 1]
    /\ free' = [free EXCEPT ![c] = free[c] - 1]
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![c] = enrolled[c] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED tok

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Courses : Enroll(i, c)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Courses : Drop(i, c)
    \/ \E c \in Courses : JoinWaitlist(c)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Courses : Promote(i, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Seats are conserved: free plus enrolled equals capacity for every course.
SeatsConserved == \A c \in Courses : free[c] + enrolled[c] = Cap
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Courses = {cs1, cs2}
    InstCount = 2
    Cap = 2
    MaxWL = 2
INVARIANT SeatsConserved
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser is backed by a small cluster of nodes that elect a single leader to own writes to the shared prescription record. Doctors submit prescription updates, which the current leader applies into the durable shared record. Once an update is present in the record, the client is told it is committed and the update becomes acknowledged. Any node may crash silently at any moment; if the crashed node was the leader, leadership falls vacant and a surviving node can be elected to take over. Crashed nodes may later recover and rejoin. The whole point of keeping the record durable across leader failover is that a committed update is never lost: an update the pharmacy has acknowledged as committed must remain present in the shared record no matter how leadership changes hands. The hazard is a failover or bookkeeping error that acknowledges an update the record does not actually hold.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every acknowledged prescription update is always still present in the shared record.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m3p1t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, Updates
NoLeader == "none"

VARIABLES leader, alive, applied, acked
vars == <<leader, alive, applied, acked>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NoLeader}
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ applied \in SUBSET Updates
    /\ acked \in SUBSET Updates

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ acked = {}

\* A live node is elected leader when the post is vacant.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, applied, acked>>

\* A node crashes silently; if it was leader, the post falls vacant.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, acked>>

\* A crashed node recovers and rejoins.
Recover(n) ==
    /\ ~alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, applied, acked>>

\* The leader applies a submitted update into the durable record.
Apply(u) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, acked>>

\* A client acknowledges an update it has observed in the record as committed.
Ack(u) ==
    /\ u \in applied
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Apply(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Ack(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No acknowledged update is ever lost from the shared record.
DurableAcks == acked \subseteq applied
=============================================================================

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker is shared by two regional hubs that both draw units from one common stock. The stock is guarded by a compare-and-swap tag: a running unit count paired with a tag that changes on every mutation. To withdraw a unit a hub must first read the current tag into its local snapshot, then commit the withdrawal, which only takes effect if the snapshot still equals the live tag. A central depot can deposit fresh units at any time, which also advances the tag and thereby invalidates any hub snapshot taken beforehand. A hub that finds its snapshot outdated can expire it and read again. Because both hubs share the same stock and the depot may move the tag between a hub's read and its commit, the compare-and-swap check is what stops a hub from mutating stock on the strength of an outdated snapshot. Every committed mutation records the tag its actor had matched. The hazard is an out-of-date hub slipping a withdrawal past the guard.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever any mutation has committed, the tag matched by the most recent actor is exactly one less than the live tag, so no hub acted on a stale snapshot.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m7p6t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Hubs, MaxTag, MaxUnits
ASSUME MaxTag \in Nat /\ MaxUnits \in Nat

NoActor == "none"
Depot == "depot"

VARIABLES units, tag, snapshot, actor, actorTag
vars == <<units, tag, snapshot, actor, actorTag>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ units \in 0..MaxUnits
    /\ tag \in 0..MaxTag
    /\ snapshot \in [Hubs -> 0..MaxTag]
    /\ actor \in Hubs \cup {NoActor, Depot}
    /\ actorTag \in 0..MaxTag

Init ==
    /\ units = 1
    /\ tag = 0
    /\ snapshot = [h \in Hubs |-> 0]
    /\ actor = NoActor
    /\ actorTag = 0

\* A hub snapshots the live tag.
ReadTag(h) ==
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![h] = tag]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<units, tag, actor, actorTag>>

\* Compare-and-swap withdrawal: succeeds only on a matching snapshot.
Withdraw(h) ==
    /\ snapshot[h] = tag
    /\ units > 0
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ units' = units - 1
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ actor' = h
    /\ actorTag' = snapshot[h]
    /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

\* The depot deposits a fresh unit, advancing the tag.
Deposit ==
    /\ units < MaxUnits
    /\ tag < MaxTag
    /\ units' = units + 1
    /\ tag' = tag + 1
    /\ actor' = Depot
    /\ actorTag' = tag
    /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

\* A hub discards an outdated snapshot.
Expire(h) ==
    /\ snapshot[h] < tag
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![h] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<units, tag, actor, actorTag>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : ReadTag(h)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : Withdraw(h)
    \/ Deposit
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : Expire(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No hub ever committed on a stale snapshot.
NoStaleWithdrawal ==
    actor # NoActor => actorTag = tag - 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Hubs = {h1, h2}
    MaxTag = 3
    MaxUnits = 2
INVARIANT NoStaleWithdrawal
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line is driven by two independent controller instances that share the one physical line. At any time at most one controller is the elected leader and is allowed to admit cars onto the conveyor; if the leader crashes, leadership falls vacant and the other controller can be elected to take over, and a crashed controller may later recover. Cars arrive and wait in a short holding queue. The leader admits a waiting car onto the conveyor only while the conveyor still has room, since the line physically holds a fixed maximum number of cars at once. Cars that reach the end of the line exit and free up space. Because both controllers feed the same line and leadership can change during a failover, the admission check is the only guard against packing more cars onto the conveyor than it can physically hold. The hazard is an admission that overfills the line.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars on the conveyor line never exceeds its fixed capacity.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m3p4t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Controllers, Cap, MaxQueue
ASSUME Cap \in Nat /\ MaxQueue \in Nat

Vacant == "vacant"

VARIABLES leader, alive, onLine, queued
vars == <<leader, alive, onLine, queued>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Controllers \cup {Vacant}
    /\ alive \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ onLine \in 0..(Cap + 2)
    /\ queued \in 0..MaxQueue

Init ==
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ alive = [c \in Controllers |-> TRUE]
    /\ onLine = 0
    /\ queued = 0

\* A live controller takes the vacant leadership.
Elect(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, onLine, queued>>

\* A controller crashes; leadership is vacated if it held it.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = c THEN Vacant ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, queued>>

\* A crashed controller recovers.
Recover(c) ==
    /\ ~alive[c]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, onLine, queued>>

\* A car arrives into the holding queue.
Arrive ==
    /\ queued < MaxQueue
    /\ queued' = queued + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, onLine>>

\* The leader admits a queued car onto the line, respecting capacity.
Admit(c) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ queued > 0
    /\ onLine < Cap
    /\ onLine' = onLine + 1
    /\ queued' = queued - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

\* A finished car exits the line.
Exit ==
    /\ onLine > 0
    /\ onLine' = onLine - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, queued>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Elect(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Recover(c)
    \/ Arrive
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Admit(c)
    \/ Exit

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The line never holds more cars than its capacity.

nl:
A print-shop job spooler runs on a small cluster that elects a leader to hand out print jobs to printer slots. The leader proposes an assignment by dropping a message onto an internal channel, and because the channel does not preserve order, these assignment messages may be applied in any sequence and stale ones may linger. An assignment is only actually applied when both the job is still unassigned and the target printer slot is still empty, at which point the spooler records the pairing in both directions: the slot remembers its job and the job remembers its slot. When a job finishes printing, both records are cleared and the slot is freed. Nodes may crash, vacating leadership for another node to pick up, and crashed nodes may recover. The danger created by reordered and stale messages is that the same job ends up wedged into two printer slots at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-job and job-to-slot records are always mutual inverses, so no job is ever assigned to two printer slots at the same time.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m3p3t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, Jobs, Printers
Vacant == "vacant"
NoJob == "nojob"
NoSlot == "noslot"

VARIABLES leader, alive, slotJob, jobSlot, msgs
vars == <<leader, alive, slotJob, jobSlot, msgs>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {Vacant}
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ slotJob \in [Printers -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]
    /\ jobSlot \in [Jobs -> Printers \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ msgs \in SUBSET (Jobs \X Printers)

Init ==
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ slotJob = [p \in Printers |-> NoJob]
    /\ jobSlot = [j \in Jobs |-> NoSlot]
    /\ msgs = {}

Elect(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, slotJob, jobSlot, msgs>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN Vacant ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotJob, jobSlot, msgs>>

Recover(n) ==
    /\ ~alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, slotJob, jobSlot, msgs>>

\* The leader proposes an assignment onto the unordered channel.
Propose(j, p) ==
    /\ leader # Vacant
    /\ jobSlot[j] = NoSlot
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {<<j, p>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, slotJob, jobSlot>>

\* An assignment message is applied only if both sides are still free.
Deliver(j, p) ==
    /\ <<j, p>> \in msgs
    /\ jobSlot[j] = NoSlot
    /\ slotJob[p] = NoJob
    /\ slotJob' = [slotJob EXCEPT ![p] = j]
    /\ jobSlot' = [jobSlot EXCEPT ![j] = p]
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {<<j, p>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

\* A finished job frees its slot and clears both records.
Complete(j) ==
    /\ jobSlot[j] # NoSlot
    /\ slotJob' = [slotJob EXCEPT ![jobSlot[j]] = NoJob]
    /\ jobSlot' = [jobSlot EXCEPT ![j] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, msgs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : Propose(j, p)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : Deliver(j, p)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Complete(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The two directional records are mutual inverses at all times.
InverseConsistent ==
    /\ \A p \in Printers : slotJob[p] # NoJob => jobSlot[slotJob[p]] = p
    /\ \A j \in Jobs : jobSlot[j] # NoSlot => slotJob[jobSlot[j]] = j
=============================================================================

nl:
A vending-machine network feeds restock tasks into a single bounded work queue that service workers drain. The queue applies backpressure: once it is full, no further task may be enqueued until a worker frees space. Authorization to drain the queue is sequenced by a monotonically advancing token: each time a worker successfully pulls and completes a task the sequence advances, so a worker must hold the current token to act. Workers sync to pick up the current token, but a slow worker that has not re-synced still holds an outdated token and is therefore stale; it is running, not failed, and simply may not process a task until it catches up. A worker can also drift and lose its synced token entirely. Every completed task records the token its worker presented. The hazard is a lagging worker draining a task on an outdated token.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever any task has been completed, the token presented by the most recent worker is exactly one less than the current authorization token, so no stale worker ever drained the queue.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m4p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Workers, MaxQ, MaxTok
ASSUME MaxQ \in Nat /\ MaxTok \in Nat

NoWorker == "none"

VARIABLES qlen, capToken, heldTok, lastWorker, lastTok
vars == <<qlen, capToken, heldTok, lastWorker, lastTok>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ qlen \in 0..MaxQ
    /\ capToken \in 0..MaxTok
    /\ heldTok \in [Workers -> 0..MaxTok]
    /\ lastWorker \in Workers \cup {NoWorker}
    /\ lastTok \in 0..MaxTok

Init ==
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ capToken = 0
    /\ heldTok = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
    /\ lastWorker = NoWorker
    /\ lastTok = 0

\* Enqueue a restock task, subject to backpressure when full.
Enqueue ==
    /\ qlen < MaxQ
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capToken, heldTok, lastWorker, lastTok>>

\* A worker syncs to the current authorization token.
Sync(w) ==
    /\ heldTok' = [heldTok EXCEPT ![w] = capToken]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, capToken, lastWorker, lastTok>>

\* A slow worker drifts and loses its synced token.
LoseSync(w) ==
    /\ heldTok[w] > 0
    /\ heldTok' = [heldTok EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, capToken, lastWorker, lastTok>>

\* A current worker drains one task; the authorization token then advances.
Process(w) ==
    /\ qlen > 0
    /\ capToken < MaxTok
    /\ heldTok[w] = capToken
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ capToken' = capToken + 1
    /\ lastWorker' = w
    /\ lastTok' = heldTok[w]
    /\ UNCHANGED heldTok

Next ==
    \/ Enqueue
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Sync(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : LoseSync(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Process(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stale worker ever drained the queue.
NoStaleDrain == lastWorker # NoWorker => lastTok = capToken - 1
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    MaxQ = 2
    MaxTok = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleDrain
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
An airport baggage router assigns bags to sorting-chute slots. Routing decisions are emitted as messages onto an internal fabric that does not preserve order, so routing messages may be applied in any sequence and old ones may still be sitting around. The router periodically reconfigures under an epoch scheme: bumping the epoch tears down all current chute assignments, forgets which bags were routed, and flushes the pending routing fabric so that decisions from the previous configuration cannot leak through. A routing message is applied only when its target chute slot is empty and the bag is not already sitting in some chute; applying it drops the bag into that slot. Bags are later unloaded from their chutes. The reordering of routing messages makes it tempting for one bag to be dropped into two different chute slots. The router must never let that happen.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct chute slots ever hold the same bag at the same time.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m9p3t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Bags, Chutes, MaxEpoch
ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat

Empty == "empty"

VARIABLES epoch, chuteBag, routed, msgs
vars == <<epoch, chuteBag, routed, msgs>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ chuteBag \in [Chutes -> Bags \cup {Empty}]
    /\ routed \in [Bags -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ msgs \in SUBSET (Bags \X Chutes)

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ chuteBag = [c \in Chutes |-> Empty]
    /\ routed = [b \in Bags |-> FALSE]
    /\ msgs = {}

\* A routing decision is emitted onto the unordered fabric.
Route(b, c) ==
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {<<b, c>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, chuteBag, routed>>

\* A routing message is applied only if the slot is empty and the bag is
\* not already routed somewhere.
Deliver(b, c) ==
    /\ <<b, c>> \in msgs
    /\ chuteBag[c] = Empty
    /\ ~routed[b]
    /\ chuteBag' = [chuteBag EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ routed' = [routed EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {<<b, c>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A bag is unloaded from its chute.
Unload(c) ==
    /\ chuteBag[c] # Empty
    /\ routed' = [routed EXCEPT ![chuteBag[c]] = FALSE]
    /\ chuteBag' = [chuteBag EXCEPT ![c] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, msgs>>

\* Epoch reconfiguration tears down all assignments and flushes the fabric.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ chuteBag' = [c \in Chutes |-> Empty]
    /\ routed' = [b \in Bags |-> FALSE]
    /\ msgs' = {}

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags, c \in Chutes : Route(b, c)
    \/ \E b \in Bags, c \in Chutes : Deliver(b, c)
    \/ \E c \in Chutes : Unload(c)
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No bag occupies two chute slots at once.
NoDoubleRoute ==
    \A c1, c2 \in Chutes :
        (chuteBag[c1] # Empty /\ chuteBag[c1] = chuteBag[c2]) => c1 = c2
=============================================================================

nl:
A subway signalling block system dispatches a train into a protected track block only after a two-phase commit across the interlocking participants that guard the surrounding switches and blocks. The coordinator opens a voting round; each participant votes yes or no. A participant may crash silently at any point, and a crashed participant may later recover. The coordinator commits the round only if every participant is alive and has voted yes; if any participant votes no, or a participant has crashed without voting, the round aborts instead. Only a committed round permits the one irreversible act: clearing the block and dispatching the train, which physically commits the movement and cannot be undone. That dispatch must fire at most once per committed round and never on an aborted one. The hazard is a signalling fault that dispatches the same movement twice or dispatches after an abort.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The irreversible train dispatch is performed at most once.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m2p5t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Participants

VARIABLES phase, votes, alive, done, fired
vars == <<phase, votes, alive, done, fired>>

Phases == {"init", "collecting", "committed", "aborted"}
Ballots == {"none", "yes", "no"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ votes \in [Participants -> Ballots]
    /\ alive \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ done \in BOOLEAN
    /\ fired \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ phase = "init"
    /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ alive = [p \in Participants |-> TRUE]
    /\ done = FALSE
    /\ fired = 0

\* Open the voting round.
Start ==
    /\ phase = "init"
    /\ phase' = "collecting"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, alive, done, fired>>

\* A live participant casts its ballot.
Vote(p, b) ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ alive[p]
    /\ votes[p] = "none"
    /\ b \in {"yes", "no"}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, alive, done, fired>>

\* A participant crashes silently.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ alive[p]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, done, fired>>

\* A crashed participant recovers.
Recover(p) ==
    /\ ~alive[p]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, done, fired>>

\* Commit only if everyone is alive and voted yes.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ \A p \in Participants : alive[p] /\ votes[p] = "yes"
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, alive, done, fired>>

\* Abort on a no-vote or a crashed unvoted participant.
Abort ==
    /\ phase = "collecting"
    /\ \E p \in Participants : votes[p] = "no" \/ (~alive[p] /\ votes[p] = "none")
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, alive, done, fired>>

\* The one irreversible dispatch, only from a committed round, only once.
Dispatch ==
    /\ phase = "committed"
    /\ ~done
    /\ done' = TRUE
    /\ fired' = fired + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, alive>>

Next ==
    \/ Start
    \/ \E p \in Participants, b \in Ballots : Vote(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Crash(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Recover(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Dispatch

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The irreversible dispatch fires at most once.
AtMostOneDispatch == fired <= 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2}
INVARIANT AtMostOneDispatch
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
An airport baggage router coordinates several nodes that occasionally need exclusive access to the router's critical reconfiguration engine. The cluster elects a single leader, and only the current leader is permitted to enter the critical section that drives the engine. A node first requests access, then enters the critical section only when it is the leader and the engine lock is free, taking the lock as it enters. When it finishes it exits, releasing the lock and returning to idle. Any node may crash silently; a crash drops its leadership if it was leader and releases the lock if it was holding it, sending that node back to idle, and a crashed node may later recover. The safety requirement is straightforward mutual exclusion: the reconfiguration engine must never be driven by two nodes at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one node is in the critical section at any time, because every node in the critical section must hold the single engine lock.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m3p0t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes
Vacant == "vacant"
Free == "free"

VARIABLES leader, lock, pcs, alive
vars == <<leader, lock, pcs, alive>>

States == {"idle", "waiting", "critical"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {Vacant}
    /\ lock \in Nodes \cup {Free}
    /\ pcs \in [Nodes -> States]
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ lock = Free
    /\ pcs = [n \in Nodes |-> "idle"]
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]

\* A live node takes vacant leadership.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, pcs, alive>>

\* An idle node asks for access.
Request(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ pcs[n] = "idle"
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![n] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, lock, alive>>

\* Only the leader may enter, and only when the lock is free.
Enter(n) ==
    /\ pcs[n] = "waiting"
    /\ leader = n
    /\ lock = Free
    /\ lock' = n
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![n] = "critical"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

\* Leave the critical section and release the lock.
Exit(n) ==
    /\ pcs[n] = "critical"
    /\ lock' = Free
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![n] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

\* Silent crash: drops leadership and lock if held.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN Vacant ELSE leader
    /\ lock' = IF lock = n THEN Free ELSE lock
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![n] = "idle"]

\* A crashed node recovers.
Recover(n) ==
    /\ ~alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, lock, pcs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Request(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Enter(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Exit(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Everyone in the critical section holds the single lock, so at most one is in.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A n \in Nodes : pcs[n] = "critical" => lock = n
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network keeps a shared access-policy record, tracking a policy version for each lock. Controller nodes push policy updates, and to prevent split-brain overwrites the system uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a fencing epoch is bumped whenever the topology changes, and a node may only push an update while the epoch it has synced to matches the live epoch. A node that has not re-synced is fenced out and cannot push. Each push advances a lock's stored policy version. Once a version is reported back to the homeowner it is confirmed for that lock. A node may crash silently, which drops its sync so it must re-sync before pushing again, and it may later recover. The durability guarantee is that a confirmed policy version is never lost: the stored version of a lock never falls below what has already been confirmed for it. The hazard is a reconfiguration or fencing bug that rolls the record back beneath a confirmed version.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every lock, the stored policy version is always at least the version already confirmed to the homeowner.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m9p1t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, Locks, MaxEpoch, MaxVer
ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat /\ MaxVer \in Nat

VARIABLES epoch, stored, confirmed, nodeEpoch, alive
vars == <<epoch, stored, confirmed, nodeEpoch, alive>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ stored \in [Locks -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ confirmed \in [Locks -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ nodeEpoch \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ stored = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ confirmed = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ nodeEpoch = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]

\* Fencing reconfiguration bumps the live epoch.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stored, confirmed, nodeEpoch, alive>>

\* A node syncs to the live epoch.
Sync(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ nodeEpoch' = [nodeEpoch EXCEPT ![n] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stored, confirmed, alive>>

\* Only a node fenced-in at the live epoch may push an update.
Push(n, l) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ nodeEpoch[n] = epoch
    /\ stored[l] < MaxVer
    /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![l] = stored[l] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, confirmed, nodeEpoch, alive>>

\* A stored version is confirmed back to the homeowner.
Confirm(l) ==
    /\ confirmed' = [confirmed EXCEPT ![l] = stored[l]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stored, nodeEpoch, alive>>

\* Silent crash drops the node's sync.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ nodeEpoch' = [nodeEpoch EXCEPT ![n] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stored, confirmed>>

\* A crashed node recovers.
Recover(n) ==
    /\ ~alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stored, confirmed, nodeEpoch>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Sync(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, l \in Locks : Push(n, l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Confirm(l)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A confirmed policy version is never lost from the stored record.
NoLostUpdate == \A l \in Locks : confirmed[l] <= stored[l]

    MaxVer = 3
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet pulls picking tasks from a single bounded work queue that applies backpressure: once the queue is full no more tasks may be enqueued until robots drain it. A central dispatcher maintains the set of robots currently authorized to pull work. Only an authorized robot may pull a task; pulling moves the task into the robot's in-flight execution and remembers who pulled it last. When the dispatcher notices a robot has fallen behind it revokes that robot's authorization, fencing it out; such a robot is slow, not failed, and is simply no longer allowed to pull, and if it happens to be the last recorded puller that stale record is cleared along with its authorization. The dispatcher can also grant authorization to a robot. Robots finish in-flight tasks over time. The hazard is a de-authorized, lagging robot still managing to pull work off the queue.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The most recent robot to have pulled a task is always still one of the currently authorized robots.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m4p6t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Robots, MaxQ, MaxInflight
ASSUME MaxQ \in Nat /\ MaxInflight \in Nat

NoRobot == "none"

VARIABLES qlen, authorized, lastPuller, inflight
vars == <<qlen, authorized, lastPuller, inflight>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ qlen \in 0..MaxQ
    /\ authorized \in SUBSET Robots
    /\ lastPuller \in Robots \cup {NoRobot}
    /\ inflight \in 0..MaxInflight

Init ==
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ authorized = {}
    /\ lastPuller = NoRobot
    /\ inflight = 0

\* Enqueue a picking task, subject to backpressure.
Enqueue ==
    /\ qlen < MaxQ
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, lastPuller, inflight>>

\* The dispatcher grants pull authorization to a robot.
Grant(r) ==
    /\ r \notin authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, lastPuller, inflight>>

\* The dispatcher fences out a lagging robot, clearing any stale record of it.
Revoke(r) ==
    /\ r \in authorized
    /\ authorized' = authorized \ {r}
    /\ lastPuller' = IF lastPuller = r THEN NoRobot ELSE lastPuller
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, inflight>>

\* Only an authorized robot may pull a task off the queue.
Pull(r) ==
    /\ r \in authorized
    /\ qlen > 0
    /\ inflight < MaxInflight
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ inflight' = inflight + 1
    /\ lastPuller' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED authorized

\* A robot finishes an in-flight task.
Complete ==
    /\ inflight > 0
    /\ inflight' = inflight - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, authorized, lastPuller>>

Next ==
    \/ Enqueue
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Grant(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Revoke(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Pull(r)
    \/ Complete

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The most recent puller is always still authorized.
AuthorizedPuller == lastPuller # NoRobot => lastPuller \in authorized
=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    MaxQ = 2
    MaxInflight = 2
INVARIANT AuthorizedPuller
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler confirms each surgery booking only after a quorum of the surgical committee has voted to approve it. Committee members cast their votes by sending them onto an internal fabric that does not preserve order, so votes may be delivered and tallied in any sequence. A vote is added to the current tally only when it is delivered. The scheduler may finalize the booking only once the tally has reached the required quorum, and it records how many approvals stood behind that confirmation. When a booking is done the scheduler opens a new round for the next surgery, which clears the tally and flushes any undelivered votes so that stale votes from the previous round cannot count. The safety requirement is that no booking is ever confirmed on the authority of fewer members than the quorum demands.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any confirmed booking was backed by at least a quorum of committee approvals.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m5p6t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Members, Quorum, MaxRound
ASSUME Quorum \in Nat /\ MaxRound \in Nat

VARIABLES tally, voteMsgs, confirmed, backing, round
vars == <<tally, voteMsgs, confirmed, backing, round>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ tally \in SUBSET Members
    /\ voteMsgs \in SUBSET Members
    /\ confirmed \in BOOLEAN
    /\ backing \in 0..Cardinality(Members)
    /\ round \in 0..MaxRound

Init ==
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ voteMsgs = {}
    /\ confirmed = FALSE
    /\ backing = 0
    /\ round = 0

\* A member casts a vote onto the unordered fabric.
CastVote(m) ==
    /\ m \notin voteMsgs
    /\ voteMsgs' = voteMsgs \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, confirmed, backing, round>>

\* A pending vote is delivered and added to the tally.
DeliverVote(m) ==
    /\ m \in voteMsgs
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {m}
    /\ voteMsgs' = voteMsgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<confirmed, backing, round>>

\* Finalize the booking only once the tally reaches quorum.
Confirm ==
    /\ ~confirmed
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
    /\ confirmed' = TRUE
    /\ backing' = Cardinality(tally)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, voteMsgs, round>>

\* Open the next round, clearing the tally and flushing stale votes.
NewRound ==
    /\ confirmed
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ voteMsgs' = {}
    /\ confirmed' = FALSE
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED backing

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker records a stream of numbered updates to its shared ledger. A writer must first take a short lease on the ledger, and the lease carries an expiry measured against a forward-only clock; the writer may only propose updates while its lease is still live. Proposed updates are pushed onto an internal channel that does not preserve order, so they may be applied to the ledger's applied-set in any sequence. Separately, the bank advances a durability high-water mark: it may extend the confirmed prefix by one only when the very next update number is already present in the applied-set, guaranteeing the confirmed prefix has no holes. When a lease expires the writer must take a fresh one before proposing again. The durability guarantee is that no update inside the confirmed prefix is ever missing from the ledger. The hazard is the high-water mark racing ahead of an update that was never actually applied.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every update number up to the confirmed high-water mark is present in the ledger's applied-set, so no confirmed update is lost.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m6p1t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Writers, N, MaxClock, LeaseLen
ASSUME N \in Nat /\ MaxClock \in Nat /\ LeaseLen \in Nat

SeqNums == 1..N
NoOwner == "none"

VARIABLES clock, leaseOwner, leaseExp, msgs, applied, confirmedUpTo
vars == <<clock, leaseOwner, leaseExp, msgs, applied, confirmedUpTo>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ leaseOwner \in Writers \cup {NoOwner}
    /\ leaseExp \in 0..(MaxClock + LeaseLen)
    /\ msgs \in SUBSET SeqNums
    /\ applied \in SUBSET SeqNums
    /\ confirmedUpTo \in 0..N

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ leaseOwner = NoOwner
    /\ leaseExp = 0
    /\ msgs = {}
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ confirmedUpTo = 0

\* Take a fresh lease on the ledger.
Lease(w) ==
    /\ leaseOwner' = w
    /\ leaseExp' = clock + LeaseLen
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, msgs, applied, confirmedUpTo>>

\* The live lease holder proposes applying an update number.
Send(w, i) ==
    /\ leaseOwner = w
    /\ leaseExp > clock
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseOwner, leaseExp, applied, confirmedUpTo>>

\* An update is applied to the ledger, possibly out of order.
Deliver(i) ==
    /\ i \in msgs
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {i}
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseOwner, leaseExp, confirmedUpTo>>

\* Extend the confirmed prefix only when the next number is already applied.
Confirm ==
    /\ confirmedUpTo < N
    /\ (confirmedUpTo + 1) \in applied
    /\ confirmedUpTo' = confirmedUpTo + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, leaseOwner, leaseExp, msgs, applied>>

\* Time advances, expiring leases.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseExp, msgs, applied, confirmedUpTo>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Writers : Lease(w)
    \/ \E w \in Writers, i \in SeqNums : Send(w, i)
    \/ \E i \in SeqNums : Deliver(i)
    \/ Confirm
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No confirmed update is missing from the ledger.
NoGap == \A i \in 1..confirmedUpTo : i \in applied
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Writers = {w1, w2}
    N = 3
    MaxClock = 3
    LeaseLen = 2
INVARIANT NoGap
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch feeds settlement instructions through a bounded work queue that applies backpressure: no new instruction may enter while the in-flight count is at its cap. A settler claims a queued instruction, but only while it is not currently busy; claiming moves the instruction into a settling state owned by that settler. Settling an instruction is irreversible: it moves real money and must happen at most once per instruction. If a settler is slow, the dispatcher may reclaim its in-flight instruction and return it to the queue for another settler; the slow settler is not failed, but its stale claim is thereby voided so it can no longer complete the settlement. Settlers toggle between busy and available over time. The hazard is a slow settler's reclaimed instruction being settled twice, once by it and once by whoever picked it up.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every settlement instruction is irreversibly settled at most once.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m4p5t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Instr, Settlers, MaxQ
ASSUME MaxQ \in Nat

NoOwner == "none"
Statuses == {"new", "queued", "settling", "settled"}

VARIABLES status, owner, settleTimes, qlen, busy
vars == <<status, owner, settleTimes, qlen, busy>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Instr -> Statuses]
    /\ owner \in [Instr -> Settlers \cup {NoOwner}]
    /\ settleTimes \in [Instr -> 0..2]
    /\ qlen \in 0..MaxQ
    /\ busy \in [Settlers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ status = [i \in Instr |-> "new"]
    /\ owner = [i \in Instr |-> NoOwner]
    /\ settleTimes = [i \in Instr |-> 0]
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ busy = [s \in Settlers |-> FALSE]

\* Submit an instruction into the bounded queue.
Submit(i) ==
    /\ status[i] = "new"
    /\ qlen < MaxQ
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "queued"]
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, settleTimes, busy>>

\* An available settler claims a queued instruction.
Claim(s, i) ==
    /\ status[i] = "queued"
    /\ ~busy[s]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "settling"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![i] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<settleTimes, qlen, busy>>

\* The owning settler irreversibly settles the instruction, once.
Settle(s, i) ==
    /\ status[i] = "settling"
    /\ owner[i] = s
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "settled"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![i] = NoOwner]
    /\ settleTimes' = [settleTimes EXCEPT ![i] = settleTimes[i] + 1]
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED busy

\* The dispatcher reclaims a slow settler's instruction, voiding its claim.
Reclaim(i) ==
    /\ status[i] = "settling"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![i] = "queued"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![i] = NoOwner]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<settleTimes, qlen, busy>>

\* A settler flips between busy and available.
ToggleBusy(s) ==
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![s] = ~busy[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, owner, settleTimes, qlen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instr : Submit(i)
    \/ \E s \in Settlers, i \in Instr : Claim(s, i)
    \/ \E s \in Settlers, i \in Instr : Settle(s, i)
    \/ \E i \in Instr : Reclaim(i)
    \/ \E s \in Settlers : ToggleBusy(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Each instruction is settled at most once.
AtMostOnceSettle == \A i \in Instr : settleTimes[i] <= 1
=============================================================================

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a fixed reserve of fuel cells. Authority to dispatch fuel circulates as a token on a ring: only the drone currently holding the token may move fuel. Every fuel cell is always in exactly one of three places: sitting in the depot, in transit as a dispatch is being flown out, or committed to airborne operations. The token holder launches a cell by sending it from the depot into transit as a dispatch message, and because the dispatch fabric does not preserve order, in-transit cells arrive and commit to airborne use in any sequence. The token holder may also land airborne fuel back into the depot. Whatever the swarm does, fuel is neither created nor destroyed: the total across the depot, the in-transit dispatches, and the airborne commitment is constant. The hazard is a dispatch bug that duplicates or drops a fuel cell.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The fuel in the depot plus the fuel in transit plus the fuel committed airborne always equals the fixed total.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m1p2t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS DroneCount, MsgIds, Total
ASSUME DroneCount \in Nat /\ Total \in Nat

Drones == 0..(DroneCount - 1)
Succ(d) == (d + 1) % DroneCount

VARIABLES token, depot, airborne, msgs
vars == <<token, depot, airborne, msgs>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Drones
    /\ depot \in 0..Total
    /\ airborne \in 0..Total
    /\ msgs \in SUBSET MsgIds

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ depot = Total
    /\ airborne = 0
    /\ msgs = {}

\* The dispatch token advances around the ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, airborne, msgs>>

\* The token holder launches a fuel cell from the depot into transit.
Launch(d) ==
    /\ token = d
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ \E g \in MsgIds :
        /\ g \notin msgs
        /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {g}
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, airborne>>

\* An in-transit cell arrives and commits to airborne use (any order).
Arrive(g) ==
    /\ g \in msgs
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {g}
    /\ airborne' = airborne + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, depot>>

\* The token holder lands airborne fuel back into the depot.
Land(d) ==
    /\ token = d
    /\ airborne > 0
    /\ airborne' = airborne - 1
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, msgs>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Launch(d)
    \/ \E g \in MsgIds : Arrive(g)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Land(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Fuel is conserved across depot, transit, and airborne.
FuelConserved == depot + Cardinality(msgs) + airborne = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    DroneCount = 2
    MsgIds = {g1, g2}
    Total = 3
INVARIANT FuelConserved
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A container-ship crane yard tracks the height of a shared container stack through a compare-and-swap register that pairs the current height with a version number. A crane must first read the current version into its local snapshot, then attempt a push or pop, which only takes effect if its snapshot still equals the live version; either operation advances the version. A push adds a container only while the stack is still below its hard capacity, and a pop removes one. A privileged yard admin has an override: the admin can lock the yard, which forbids any further pushes, and can clear the stack outright in an emergency, resetting the height and bumping the version. The compare-and-swap check keeps concurrent cranes from stepping on each other, and the capacity guard keeps the stack from being overfilled. The hazard is a push that drives the stack past its physical capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The container stack height never exceeds the yard's fixed capacity.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m7p4t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cranes, Cap, MaxVer
ASSUME Cap \in Nat /\ MaxVer \in Nat

VARIABLES height, version, snap, locked
vars == <<height, version, snap, locked>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ height \in 0..(Cap + 2)
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ snap \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ locked \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ height = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ locked = FALSE

\* A crane snapshots the live version.
ReadVer(c) ==
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<height, version, locked>>

\* Compare-and-swap push, respecting the lock and the capacity.
Push(c) ==
    /\ ~locked
    /\ snap[c] = version
    /\ height < Cap
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ height' = height + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, locked>>

\* Compare-and-swap pop.
Pop(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] = version
    /\ height > 0
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ height' = height - 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, locked>>

\* Admin emergency clear.
AdminClear ==
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ height' = 0
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, locked>>

\* Admin lock toggle.
AdminLock ==
    /\ locked' = ~locked
    /\ UNCHANGED <<height, version, snap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : ReadVer(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Push(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Pop(c)
    \/ AdminClear
    \/ AdminLock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The stack never exceeds capacity.
YardWithinCapacity == height <= Cap
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {c1, c2}
    Cap = 3
    MaxVer = 4
INVARIANT YardWithinCapacity
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A subway signalling block system guards a single critical junction that only one train may occupy at a time. A cluster of dispatcher nodes elects a leader, and only while a leader is in office may a train be moved into the junction. Trains approach and queue for the junction. The line has a capacity that operations staff change at runtime, raising or lowering how much traffic the line will accept; a train may only be moved into the critical junction while the line capacity is above zero and the junction is currently empty. When a train clears the junction it departs and the junction frees up. Dispatcher nodes may crash, vacating leadership until another node is elected, and crashed nodes may recover. The absolute safety requirement, regardless of leadership churn or capacity changes, is that the junction is never occupied by two trains at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct trains are ever in the critical junction at the same time.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m3p0t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, Trains, MaxCap
ASSUME MaxCap \in Nat

Vacant == "vacant"
TrainStates == {"idle", "queued", "injunction"}

VARIABLES leader, alive, pcs, cap
vars == <<leader, alive, pcs, cap>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {Vacant}
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ pcs \in [Trains -> TrainStates]
    /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ pcs = [t \in Trains |-> "idle"]
    /\ cap = MaxCap

Elect(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ leader = Vacant
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, pcs, cap>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN Vacant ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pcs, cap>>

Recover(n) ==
    /\ ~alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, pcs, cap>>

\* Operations staff change the line capacity at runtime.
SetCap(k) ==
    /\ k \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, pcs>>

\* A train approaches and queues.
Approach(t) ==
    /\ pcs[t] = "idle"
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![t] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, cap>>

\* Move a queued train into the empty junction, under a leader and capacity.
Enter(t) ==
    /\ pcs[t] = "queued"
    /\ leader # Vacant
    /\ cap > 0
    /\ \A u \in Trains : pcs[u] # "injunction"
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![t] = "injunction"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, cap>>

\* A train clears the junction and departs.
Depart(t) ==
    /\ pcs[t] = "injunction"
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)
    \/ \E k \in 0..MaxCap : SetCap(k)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Approach(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Enter(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Depart(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No two trains ever share the critical junction.
JunctionMutex ==
    \A t1, t2 \in Trains :
        (pcs[t1] = "injunction" /\ pcs[t2] = "injunction") => t1 = t2
=============================================================================

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line applies a final wax coat to each car, an irreversible step that must happen at most once per car. Workers use optimistic locking with retry against a shared configuration version. A worker first snapshots the current config version for a car, marking it ready. It then finalizes the wax only if its snapshot still matches the live config version and a wash bay is available; a finalize is irreversible and is refused if the car has already been finalized. If the configuration changes between the snapshot and the finalize, the optimistic check fails and the car is sent back to be re-read and retried. The configuration version can be bumped at runtime, and separately the number of active wash bays, the line capacity, can be raised or lowered at runtime. The hazard is a stale or duplicated finalize that waxes the same car twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every car has its irreversible wax finalize applied at most once.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m0p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cars, MaxVer, MaxCap
ASSUME MaxVer \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat

Phases == {"queued", "ready", "done"}

VARIABLES version, snap, fin, cap, phase
vars == <<version, snap, fin, cap, phase>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ snap \in [Cars -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ fin \in [Cars -> 0..2]
    /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ phase \in [Cars -> Phases]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ fin = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ cap = MaxCap
    /\ phase = [c \in Cars |-> "queued"]

\* Snapshot the config version for a car (start of the optimistic attempt).
Snapshot(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "queued"
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "ready"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, fin, cap>>

\* Configuration is bumped at runtime, invalidating outstanding snapshots.
BumpConfig ==
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, fin, cap, phase>>

\* Wash-bay capacity changes at runtime.
SetCap(k) ==
    /\ k \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snap, fin, phase>>

\* Irreversible finalize: only on a matching snapshot, with capacity, once.
Finalize(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "ready"
    /\ snap[c] = version
    /\ fin[c] = 0
    /\ cap > 0
    /\ fin' = [fin EXCEPT ![c] = fin[c] + 1]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snap, cap>>

\* Optimistic check failed: send the car back to retry.
Retry(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "ready"
    /\ snap[c] # version
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snap, fin, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Snapshot(c)
    \/ BumpConfig
    \/ \E k \in 0..MaxCap : SetCap(k)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Finalize(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Retry(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The irreversible wax finalize happens at most once per car.
FinalizeAtMostOnce == \A c \in Cars : fin[c] <= 1
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {k1, k2}
    MaxVer = 2
    MaxCap = 2
INVARIANT FinalizeAtMostOnce
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A print-shop job spooler hands out printers to workers under short leases that carry an expiry against a forward-only clock. A worker may print on a printer only while it actually holds that printer's lease and the lease has not expired. A worker holding a live lease may renew it or use it to print, and each print records which worker performed it on that printer. A lease can be re-acquired by another worker once it is free or has lapsed, and re-acquiring evicts any stale record of who last printed there. A privileged shop admin has an override that can forcibly reassign any printer to any worker, likewise clearing the stale print record. A worker whose lease has lapsed or been taken over is stale and must not be recorded as the printer of a machine now owned by someone else. The hazard is a lagging worker's print slipping onto a printer it no longer legitimately holds.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every printer, if a worker is recorded as its last printer then that worker is the printer's current lease owner, so no stale worker's print is ever attributed to a reassigned printer.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m6p6t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Workers, Printers, MaxClock, LeaseLen
ASSUME MaxClock \in Nat /\ LeaseLen \in Nat

Nobody == "nobody"

VARIABLES clock, owner, expiry, printedBy
vars == <<clock, owner, expiry, printedBy>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ owner \in [Printers -> Workers \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ expiry \in [Printers -> 0..(MaxClock + LeaseLen)]
    /\ printedBy \in [Printers -> Workers \cup {Nobody}]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ owner = [p \in Printers |-> Nobody]
    /\ expiry = [p \in Printers |-> 0]
    /\ printedBy = [p \in Printers |-> Nobody]

Lapsed(p) == owner[p] = Nobody \/ expiry[p] <= clock

\* Acquire a free or lapsed printer, evicting any stale print record.
Acquire(w, p) ==
    /\ Lapsed(p)
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![p] = w]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![p] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ printedBy' = [printedBy EXCEPT ![p] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* Renew a live lease.
Renew(w, p) ==
    /\ owner[p] = w
    /\ expiry[p] > clock
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![p] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, owner, printedBy>>

\* Print only under a live lease held by this worker.
Print(w, p) ==
    /\ owner[p] = w
    /\ expiry[p] > clock
    /\ printedBy' = [printedBy EXCEPT ![p] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, owner, expiry>>

\* Admin override: forcibly reassign a printer, clearing the stale record.
AdminReassign(w, p) ==
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![p] = w]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![p] = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ printedBy' = [printedBy EXCEPT ![p] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, expiry, printedBy>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers, p \in Printers : Acquire(w, p)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, p \in Printers : Renew(w, p)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, p \in Printers : Print(w, p)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, p \in Printers : AdminReassign(w, p)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A recorded printer is always the printer's current lease owner.
NoStalePrint ==
    \A p \in Printers : printedBy[p] # Nobody => owner[p] = printedBy[p]
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {u1, u2}
    Printers = {p1, p2}
    MaxClock = 2
    LeaseLen = 2
INVARIANT NoStalePrint
SPECIFICATION Spec

nl:
A power-grid load shedder can perform one drastic, irreversible act: tripping a critical breaker to shed load. Authority to trip circulates as a token on a ring of control nodes, and only the node currently holding the token may trip. The token advances around the ring from one node to the next. Any node may crash silently; if the crashed node was holding the token, the token is dropped and becomes unheld until a surviving node reclaims it. Crashed nodes may later recover and rejoin. Only a live node holding the token may trip, and the trip is irreversible: once the breaker has been tripped it must never be tripped a second time. The hazard is a token-handoff or crash-recovery glitch that fires the irreversible trip more than once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The irreversible breaker trip is performed at most once.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m1p5t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS NodeCount
ASSUME NodeCount \in Nat

Nodes == 0..(NodeCount - 1)

VARIABLES token, held, alive, tripped, fired
vars == <<token, held, alive, tripped, fired>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Nodes
    /\ held \in BOOLEAN
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ tripped \in BOOLEAN
    /\ fired \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ held = TRUE
    /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ tripped = FALSE
    /\ fired = 0

\* The token advances one step around the ring.
PassToken ==
    /\ held
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % NodeCount
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, alive, tripped, fired>>

\* A node crashes silently, dropping the token if it held it.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ held' = IF held /\ token = n THEN FALSE ELSE held
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, tripped, fired>>

\* A crashed node recovers.
Recover(n) ==
    /\ ~alive[n]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, held, tripped, fired>>

\* A live node reclaims an unheld token.
Reclaim(n) ==
    /\ ~held
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ held' = TRUE
    /\ token' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, tripped, fired>>

\* The irreversible trip, only by a live token holder, only once.
Trip(n) ==
    /\ held
    /\ token = n
    /\ alive[n]
    /\ ~tripped
    /\ tripped' = TRUE
    /\ fired' = fired + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, held, alive>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm is flown as two fleets that share one critical comms-relay channel. Access to the relay is arbitrated by a compare-and-swap lock register that names either the current holder or a free marker, together with a generation counter. A drone first observes the register into its local snapshot. It then attempts a compare-and-swap acquire, which succeeds only if its snapshot showed free and the register is in fact still free; a successful acquire installs the drone as holder, moves it into the critical section, and advances the generation. If the snapshot was stale because someone else grabbed the relay first, the attempt fails and the drone re-observes to retry. A holder releases the relay when done, freeing the register. Because both fleets contend for the same relay, the compare-and-swap arbitration is what enforces exclusive use. The hazard is two drones believing they both hold the relay at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A drone is in the critical section if and only if the lock register names it, so at most one drone ever holds the relay.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m7p0t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Drones, Modulus
ASSUME Modulus \in Nat

Free == "free"

VARIABLES casReg, pcs, snap, gen
vars == <<casReg, pcs, snap, gen>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ casReg \in Drones \cup {Free}
    /\ pcs \in [Drones -> {"idle", "critical"}]
    /\ snap \in [Drones -> Drones \cup {Free}]
    /\ gen \in 0..(Modulus - 1)

Init ==
    /\ casReg = Free
    /\ pcs = [d \in Drones |-> "idle"]
    /\ snap = [d \in Drones |-> Free]
    /\ gen = 0

\* Observe the register into a local snapshot.
Observe(d) ==
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![d] = casReg]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<casReg, pcs, gen>>

\* Compare-and-swap acquire: succeeds only if snapshot and register are free.
Acquire(d) ==
    /\ pcs[d] = "idle"
    /\ snap[d] = Free
    /\ casReg = Free
    /\ casReg' = d
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![d] = "critical"]
    /\ gen' = (gen + 1) % Modulus
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* Release the relay, freeing the register.
Release(d) ==
    /\ casReg = d
    /\ casReg' = Free
    /\ pcs' = [pcs EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, gen>>

\* CAS failed (snapshot stale): re-observe to retry.
Retry(d) ==
    /\ snap[d] = Free
    /\ casReg # Free
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![d] = casReg]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<casReg, pcs, gen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Observe(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Acquire(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Release(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Retry(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A drone is critical iff the register names it: at most one holder.
MutexCoherent ==
    \A d \in Drones : (pcs[d] = "critical") <=> (casReg = d)
=============================================================================
